- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often overshoots downward; avoid sharp drops; adjust downward only if sentiment persists.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +0.5+ in sentiment) by forecasting higher prices for 3–5 days; cap peak forecasts at 1–2% above recent high.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to overestimate volatility in early days (1–7) and undercorrects in late days (24–30); apply smoothing or decay factor to later days.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model often misses the rebound; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias in 3–5 days after sentiment turns positive.
